chunks: Ali ibn Ja'far narrated from his brother who said:

I asked him about the man who prays facing the Qibla but is not considered reliable (in religious matters); he brought a drink and claimed that it is one-third (wine and two-thirds water), so is its drinking permissible? He said: 'He is not believed unless he is a Muslim who is well-versed (in the rules of wine and water mixture).'
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a person to be believed when claiming a drink is permissible (one-third wine)?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a person’s general piety or regular prayer is insufficient to validate their claim regarding the permissibility of a beverage mixed with wine; they must possess specific expertise in the fiqh of *khumur*. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on *'adl* (justice/integrity) combined with *'ilm* (specialized knowledge) when accepting testimonies in matters of ritual purity and consumption. It highlights the distinction between general religious observance and the technical competence required to interpret legal nuances in food and drink.
